issues.description: The substantial Stata preparation program is printed inside Lester_Code_Description.pdf rather than supplied as an executable .do file. Extract a working copy and compare wrapped/page-split statements against the PDF before an authorized run.

H1 labels its quarter map abbreviated/example, saves pooled cohorts for 2004, 2007, and 2010, and appends a 2005–2013 range whose producer blocks are absent from supplied text. Obtain omitted builders or confirm separately supplied intermediates; do not invent cohorts.

The source ends by cleaning log_compen and log_for_emp but shows no producers or imported table schema. They may be inherited from an undocumented source; the code excerpt does not prove they are absent from all inputs.

Code loads capex and employees as separate aliases, but their source producers/schema and date coverage are undocumented. Similar Compustat field names are candidates until merge contracts are confirmed.

DPAD, NOL, Hoopes R&D credit, and Dyreng Exhibit 21 inputs have distinct sources and histories. Compatible author-prepared tables and exact schemas/rules/coverage must be established; historical assistance is not by itself a current NDA barrier.

evidence.description: The datasheet states that the BEA records are confidential and restricted to researchers with Special Sworn Employee status. This supports an unverified current access route, not a finding that this worker lacks eligibility.
evidence.quote:
I used confidential data on U.S. multinational firms from the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. These
   data can only be accessed by researchers who have received Special Sworn Employee status. Contact
   information for the BEA employees that oversee the Special Sworn Employee program has been
   provided to the editors at the same time as this final data description.

evidence.description: The datasheet describes DPAD firm identification as financial-statement search followed by manual review/coding.
evidence.quote:
Dataset identifying DPAD Firms: To identify the DPAD firms studied in this paper, I created a list of
   search terms (listed in Appendix A of the manuscript) and provided this list to Jeff Hoopes, who created
   a Perl program for me in April 2014 to search annual financial statements. I personally reviewed each
   excerpt and coded each match so as to correctly identify firms that discuss or disclose the benefit and
   the first financial statement year in which the terms are identified. Excerpts range from a general
   discussion of the benefit in any section of a firm’s financial statements to disclosure of the specific
   amount of DPAD benefit in a firm’s effective tax rate reconciliation. I disclose Jeff’s assistance in the
   Acknowledgements section of the paper.

review_notes: The frozen dependency list is empty, but the printed program contains explicit use, merge, and append reads. Manual source inspection recorded external reads as data requirements and distinguished generated intermediates from supplied inputs.
Static code-parser zero is not evidence that the package has no code: extracted PDF text contains a substantial printed Stata .do program. The package has no standalone .do file.
Table-producing estimator code is not included in the supplied PDF; this is a contextual limitation outside the selected preparation/matching scope.

H1 source shows an abbreviated/example quarter map, explicit 2004/2007/2010 pooled producers, and an append range for 2005–2013 with no visible producer blocks for that sequence; treat these as unresolved source/intermediate contracts.

H2 annual and segment products for 2013–2017 are separate from Compustat/segment history 1995–2013. The extension code drops 2012 and 2017; longer intermediate leads do not establish longer future outcome horizons.

H3a and H3b consume restricted BEA company-level domestic records; H3a also reads a separate foreign BEA file. Public BEA aggregates cannot replace these private inputs. Current individual secure-site access remains unknown.
DPAD, NOL, Hoopes rdchand, and Dyreng Exhibit 21 are distinct input contracts with different sources and histories. Historical researcher assistance is not treated as a current NDA barrier.
The supplied Sample Firm Identifiers workbook is a one-column identifier list, not an analysis panel or proof of linked data coverage.
The appendix discusses ETI, positive shocks, and Hanlon repatriator data, but no consumer appears in supplied program; they remain context, not invented requirements.
One-row Compustat and root-only SEC/LM probes are candidates only and do not establish required coverage. Raw/parsed filing roots do not prove processed DPAD, NOL, or Exhibit 21 panels.
